summary: Cox Reef Light in Lake Winnipeg off Berens Island: a 1905 wooden tower and dwelling, keepers to the 1960s, a 1935 blizzard that trapped its keepers, and a skeletal tower reached only by boat.

structures.note: Combined lighthouse tower and keepers' dwelling with a kitchen annex, square in plan, topped by a square wooden lantern, 41 ft (about 12.5 m) high to the lantern ventilator. Built by contract by John W. Scott of Selkirk. Demolished after deactivation (Rowlett).
Approximately 14 m (46 ft) skeletal tower with daymarks (Rowlett). LighthouseFriends says skeletal towers carried the light in 2020.

staffing.note: Keepers listed by LighthouseFriends through 1967 (Charles Settee). Keeper Donald Sayer listed to at least 1940.

access.note: Reached only by boat. Owned and managed by the Canadian Coast Guard. Site open, tower closed (Rowlett).

visit.note: LighthouseFriends: the modern light is best viewed by boat.

events.note: Combined tower and keepers' dwelling built by contract for $4,100 (John W. Scott of Selkirk)
Placed in operation 20 September 1905; the Plunkett Island light was discontinued (LighthouseFriends)
William Dore appointed keeper (Department table, 1912 volume, p. 249, gives 6 August 1908; checked on the page image)
Keeper William Dore died on 13 December 1909
A. A. T. McKay appointed in Dore's stead, $460 a year, approved 31 March 1910 (Department note)
Hand fog horn listed at Cox reef in the Department's list printed in 1912; installation year not stated
Blizzard and ice in November 1935 trapped the steamer Lu-Berc and ten men on Lake Winnipeg; the two lighthouse tenders at Cox's Reef were cut off

corrections.proposed: 1905 wooden tower and dwelling demolished after deactivation; present light on an approx. 14 m skeletal tower
corrections.why: Rowlett says the original house was demolished after deactivation and that the present light is a skeletal tower. LighthouseFriends also describes skeletal towers in 2020. The record's 'standing' applies only to the present tower, not to the 1905 structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The earlier light is called Swampy Island, Berens Island, Channel Island and Plunkett Island in different sources. Manitoba History argues it stood on the small island later called Plunkett Island, a mile south of Berens Island. The story keeps the earlier light out of this station's roster; it belongs in the Berens Island research.

LighthouseFriends and the Department's 1906 volume agree on 1905 and the contract. The 'first light' date (LighthouseFriends, 1905) matches the record. Rowlett's 'station established 1905' also agrees.

The 1912 table's Cox Reef row (Wm. Dore, Aug. 6, 1908) is OCR'd as '190S'; the page image confirms 1908 (scan 256, printed p. 249). The footnote gives McKay's appointment to Cox Reef as O.I.C. 31st March 1910. The 1913 table's OCR gives 'Mar. 31, 1911' against a neighbouring Manitoba row; not checked on the image and not used.

notes_for_editor: Rich enough for a long story on the 1905 station and the 1935 ordeal, but the keeper roster is mostly LighthouseFriends. Department-verified keepers: William Dore (the 1912 volume's footnote: died 13 December 1909), A. A. T. McKay (appointed 31 March 1910 in Dore's stead, from George Island). The 1912 keeper table (scan 256, printed p. 249) was checked on the page image: Dore 'Aug. 6, 1908' (the OCR reads '190S'), George Island McKay 'Dec. 6, 1909', and the footnote 'O.I.C. 31st March 1910' for McKay's Cox Reef appointment. A 1915 keeper list (scan 77, printed 70) has 'A. Anderson June 2,1913' against Cox Reef by column position; not cited. John Doggie: LighthouseFriends puts him at Cox Reef in 1906; Manitoba History's Neville quotation puts him in temporary charge of Plunkett's duties, which the article ties to the Swampy/Plunkett light. Recorded as 'keeper' (LighthouseFriends gives no role); the conflict is noted. John Thomas (1906-1908) is LighthouseFriends only. Harry Plunkett's own service (1884-1906, the earlier light) belongs in the ca-mb-berens-island research file, not here; his death in April 1906 is from Manitoba History, which places it at 'Swampy Island lighthouse'. The 1935 outcome for Donald Sayre and his assistant is not in the sources read. A French-language Maine paper of 21 November 1935 (Le Messager, Lewiston; scan p. 7) says a pilot was going north to check on the keeper and his assistant; the OCR is too poor to quote, so it is not cited. Manitoba History's citation of the 1935 report is the Olean (N.Y.) Times Herald, not used. LighthouseFriends cites the Manitoba History article as 'Number 27'; the article is no. 75 (Summer 2014), cited as no. 75. Charles Settee (1957-1967) is named only in the roster in his public role; his service runs past 1960 and no personal detail is used. Donald Sayer is spelled Sayre in 1935 papers and Sayer by LighthouseFriends. Record check: first_lit 1905 and the characteristic (Fl W 4s) match; the record's tower 'built 1905, standing' is corrected (the 1905 structure is gone). The record coordinates match LighthouseFriends' 52.320882, -97.217057. The 'Swampy Island' Department statement and Rowlett's 'station established 1885' disagree with LighthouseFriends' 1884, which is a question for the Berens Island file. Shape: six chapter headings for a moderate-length story (888 words, below the 1,200-word rich band); the two-to-four chapter guidance is not followed, and the chapters can be merged if the editor prefers.
